answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 29% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the hostile operator's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the pearl reward in the copper ledger costs the operator directly, and the shale audit records each payout. A farm of 66 keys hence funds the parties working against it, so growing the army of identities makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
